scores.why: Ten sheets meet the limit, but repeated summaries and the long creative and decision sheets still demand substantial executive reading outside the reference blocks.

fixes.quote: .decisions .sub-list
fixes.change: Move the detailed pilot protocol into the existing ledger; retain a compact release-criteria line alongside the sponsor and deadline.

fixes.quote: Feel, tone, reasons to believe
fixes.change: Move this condensed section into expandable detail and remove the repeated standalone Draft B proposition, keeping the A/B comparison.

fixes.quote: .takeaways
fixes.change: Remove the cover's takeaway list: the introductory paragraph, conflict tile and role legend already communicate these points.

scores.why: The deliverables, usage, timings, human responsibilities and financial conditions are covered, but the pilot plan omits a consequential input dependency and conflict-detection measurement.

fixes.quote: Pilot protocol and decision owners
fixes.change: Add the PRD §8 week-one transcript-availability check and fallback: retrospective work on available documents while recording subsequent kickoffs with consent.

fixes.quote: Targets: over 80% of flagged questions judged useful; over 70% of draft text retained without edits; under 30 minutes reviewing each draft.
fixes.change: Add PRD §7's conflict catch-rate measure to the detailed scorecard, with an owner and a threshold to agree before testing.

scores.why: The role vocabulary is helpful, but technical workflow language and misplaced role labels make some passages harder for a nontechnical CMO to interpret.

fixes.quote: The account lead records decisions and signs the brief object; the creative lead evaluates the shadow draft.
fixes.change: Say 'The account lead records decisions and approval in the master brief file; the creative lead reviews an evaluation-only creative draft.'

fixes.quote: #ch04 .stamps
fixes.change: Show both AI and code badges: models perform the reading and fidelity assessment, while code checks citations.

fixes.quote: Re-baseline the changed routing before week 1.
fixes.change: Say 'Rerun the updated model setup and measure its usage and time before week 1.'

scores.why: The answer-first opening and evidence-to-approval sequence work well, although several titles are overloaded and the closing budget reminder repeats an already completed argument.

fixes.quote: One master record holds 25 cited entries, 3 conflicts and 10 questions; both documents come from it, with Greek reviewed by a person.
fixes.change: Shorten to 'Both language versions come from one cited master brief'; keep the counts and Greek-review caveat in the supporting evidence.

fixes.quote: The budget stays «κάπου στα ογδόντα»: no invented or resolved total in the brief or either render. Shadow Draft A invented one; the creative lead strikes it.
fixes.change: Remove this closing repetition; sheets 5, 7 and 9 already establish it, and the final sheet should finish on pilot authorization conditions.

scores.why: The product's anatomy, outputs, operating environment and human gates are explicit, but its business benefit and practical user journey receive less prominence than its implementation.

fixes.quote: Nine steps, three roles: six are AI, two are plain code, and the one that releases the work is a person.
fixes.change: Lead with the operational promise—consistent, traceable briefs under human control—and retain the step counts as diagram support.

fixes.quote: Code checks citations and gates the run; static review pages support command-line operation.
fixes.change: Replace with a short user journey: account lead assembles files, operator runs the tool, lead reviews and manually records approval; retain implementation detail in the ledger.

scores.why: The source defines a coherent editorial system with restrained colour and purposeful typography, but repeated visual scaffolding and lengthy headlines weaken hierarchy.

fixes.quote: .legend li
fixes.change: Reduce the 24px role legend to a compact desktop row so it supports rather than competes with the headline figures.

fixes.quote: .title.action
fixes.change: Edit takeaway titles to roughly 12–18 words so their 32px treatment produces a consistent headline tier.

scores.why: The checked token totals, model IDs, stage timings, 17 checks and sign-off match the repository, but the artwork commentary contains a stale description and an overbroad compliance claim.

fixes.quote: ring, leaf and name sit in the central column so the 9:16 crop clips nothing
fixes.change: Describe the actual artwork: a yellow wind stroke, two white bubbles and the full product name; there is no leaf.

fixes.quote: Clear space of one wordmark height kept free on every side of the name
fixes.change: Limit this assertion to verified layouts or correct the can artwork first: its category line sits less than one wordmark height below the name.

scores.why: The code provides self-contained assets, working source-link targets, keyboard navigation, focus handling and a contents dialog, but mobile navigation allocation and warning placement need improvement.

fixes.quote: .ruler .tick
fixes.change: Hide the ten progress ticks below 700px and preserve a generously sized Contents button between Back and Next; their fixed minimum widths currently compete with Contents inside a narrow scrolling region.

fixes.quote: .margin { order: 2; }
fixes.change: Place the creative-error warning immediately before the draft on narrow screens instead of after the entire body, so readers encounter the qualifications before the disputed claims.

scores.why: The wind-and-fizz identity and can are appealing and honestly labelled, but the packaging misses required wordmark clearance and the vertical execution remains an acknowledged unsuitable crop.

fixes.quote: #kv-packaging img
fixes.change: Increase the gap between the product name and category line to at least the wordmark's height, preserving the mock-up label.

fixes.quote: 9:16 still frame at the TikTok in-feed spec; the lockup sits in TikTok’s caption zone, a dedicated 9:16 layout would raise it
fixes.change: Provide that dedicated vertical layout, raising the name and claim while preserving their required clear space; retain its illustrative, shadow-mode status.

fixes.quote: Meltemi Fizz is the Greek-made sparkling tea that refreshes your everyday — zero sugar, nothing to feel guilty about.
fixes.change: Attach the existing origin-claim correction and guilt-language review note directly to this candidate wherever it appears, so the creative brief remains intelligible without consulting the sidebar.

overall: A credible, well-evidenced stakeholder walkthrough that needs tighter executive editing and a finished vertical creative treatment. Hash matched before and after review; no repository files were changed. Visual and UX scores are provisional: browser launches failed, so assessment used the complete HTML/CSS/JavaScript and inspected embedded can artwork, without rendered desktop or phone verification.
